name: Make It Posh!

pick.label: Pick something ordinary
pick.heading: Pick something ordinary and turn it into a luxury brand
lead: Luxury brands can sell almost anything for a fortune: a T-shirt, a candle, a paper clip. The product often matters less than the story, the shop, the price and the people who are seen with it.
Choose something completely ordinary and turn it into a luxury brand. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The more boring the thing, the better.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a serious business plan, this is just for fun. Some of the best luxury brands in history started with something just as ordinary, so who knows.

rows: Which ordinary thing are you turning into luxury?
Something that sounds expensive. French, Italian, a made-up family name, one mysterious word…
Every luxury brand needs a heritage story. Invent one.
How much? Remember, if it’s too cheap, nobody will believe it’s luxury.
Who would pay that much, and why? Be honest, but kind.
Where? A boutique on Kurfürstendamm, a secret shop with no sign, by invitation only…

values.name: Leitung. One word, no explanation, small grey letters on a very heavy glass bottle with a cork.
values.story: It has flowed through the same Berlin pipes since the days of the Kaiser, according to me, which I am choosing to call heritage.
values.price: €14 a bottle, or €40 if you want it from one particular district. Friedrichshain is the most expensive, obviously, because that’s where I live.
values.who: People with lots of money and little sense, and anybody trying to impress a date who knows nothing about wine.
values.where: A tiny shop in Mitte with no sign and one bottle in the window. You need an appointment, and they will make you wait twenty minutes anyway.

yours.label: Your luxury brand
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your luxury brand in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which luxury brand wins?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their luxury brand in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
